subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw core own an integrated opt-in safe-update transaction that snapshots state, runs real post-update checks, and restores or rolls back on failure?
rationale: The remaining gap defines updater product scope, secret handling, restore semantics, retention, and live smoke criteria across core state and plugins, which automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Safe Update
options.body: Define a default-off core workflow with explicit snapshot contents, retention, smoke criteria, rollback ordering, and secret-safe restore policy.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Canonical Issues
options.body: Track backup/restore, compatibility scanner, auto-update, and rollback pieces separately before approving an integrated updater transaction.

options.title: Keep Outside Core For Now
options.body: Document community kits and manual recovery while declining a core transaction until the updater scope is clearer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Safe Update
recommendation.body: Define a default-off core workflow with explicit snapshot contents, retention, smoke criteria, rollback ordering, and secret-safe restore policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product scope and safety policy, and prior issue discussion points to this reviewer as the best available routing owner.
